sandbox.title: Physics sandbox
sandbox.subtitle: Run isolated Newtonian experiments. Each preset resets to its own exact initial state.
sandbox.impactEnergyModelled: Estimated from the catalogue impact speed before the collision.
sandbox.impactEnergyActual: Recalculated from the simulated impact speed.
sandbox.airburstFlag: The impact module heuristic flags possible airburst conditions.
sandbox.airburstUnsupported: The gas giant has no solid-surface model; atmospheric burst effects are not estimated.
sandbox.noAirburstFlag: The impact module heuristic does not flag airburst conditions.

validity.valid: Far-field range: Newtonian approximation marked valid by the model gauge.
validity.caution: Caution: Newtonian approximation is increasingly limited here.
validity.invalid: Outside the stated range of the Newtonian approximation.

notes.stable: JPL Solar System initial conditions, integrated with the app's fixed-step Newtonian engine.
notes.twoBody: Sun and Earth initial state from JPL; other bodies are omitted for this two-body experiment.
notes.impact: Earth and a 500 m radius, 3000 kg/mВі illustrative asteroid. Impact energy and the airburst flag use the impact module. The N-body engine does not resolve body contact, an atmospheric trajectory, or damage.
notes.starReplacement: Instantly replaces the Sun's gravitational parameter with half its initial value while preserving all positions and velocities. This is a controlled thought experiment, not stellar evolution.
notes.blackHole: A 1000 solar-mass non-rotating black hole and a test particle at 12 Schwarzschild radii. Newtonian particle motion is only an approximation; see the validity gauge.
notes.empty: An empty simulation clock with no bodies. Conservation diagnostics are undefined.

sandbox.starModelCard: Model Card В· Instantaneous mass substitution. Other bodies keep their positions and velocities. No stellar evolution, mass loss, ejecta, or radiation is modelled.
sandbox.blackHoleModelCard: Model Card В· Non-rotating Schwarzschild geometry for radius and gauge; test-particle trajectory remains Newtonian. No relativistic trajectory or light propagation.
sandbox.impactModelCard: Model Card В· Spherical uniform-density impactor and Newtonian kinetic energy. Body contact is not resolved. Airburst output is a coarse heuristic, not a probability or damage forecast.
sandbox.newtonianModelCard: Model Card В· Point-mass Newtonian gravity with a fixed-step velocity-Verlet integrator. Scene geometry is illustrative and not to scale.
sandbox.assumptions: Assumed because the record has no value: {list}.
sandbox.unverified: Catalogue values are approximate and unverified.
sandbox.catalogNote: Scenario built from the catalogue record. It uses the same simplified Newtonian engine as the presets; see the model card below for limits.
sandbox.collisionBody: The body reached {target} after {days} d at {speed} km/s. The run is stopped; press reset to repeat.

lab.title: Simulation labs
lab.subtitle: Pick a model, then run it with a preset or with an object from the catalogue.

star-replacement.title: Star replacement
star-replacement.body: Swap the Sun for another star mass and watch whether the planets stay bound.
star-replacement.limit: Newtonian gravity only: no stellar evolution, no luminosity or climate model.

impact.title: Impact
impact.body: Send an asteroid or comet at Earth: kinetic energy, TNT equivalent, airburst flag, and a stop when the body reaches Earth.
impact.limit: No crater, blast or casualty model; energy figures are a simple kinetic estimate.

black-hole.title: Black hole
black-hole.body: Orbit a test particle around a black hole at 12 Schwarzschild radii, with a validity gauge for the Newtonian approximation.
black-hole.limit: Newtonian approximation, not general relativity; no lensing, no spin.

sandbox.title: Build your own
sandbox.body: Place your own bodies and watch them orbit; energy and angular-momentum drift are shown live.
sandbox.limit: Planar start, point masses, no collisions between your bodies.

scale.label: Scale
scale.galaxyNote: 1 unit = 500 light-years. Directions and distances of listed objects are real; the spiral arms are illustrative, not a measured map.
scale.universeNote: Directions are real; distances are compressed and galaxy sizes exaggerated so everything fits. Not to scale.

gallery.title: Experiments you can run right now
gallery.subtitle: Pick a ready-made scenario and it opens in the simulator immediately. Every value comes from the catalog and is labelled as an estimate; nothing here is a prediction.
gallery.communityEmpty: Nobody has published an experiment yet. Save one in the sandbox and share it.
gallery.communityOffline: Community experiments are unavailable right now (database not connected). The ready-made ones above work normally.

stable-system.title: Stable Solar System
stable-system.body: Sun and planets from real initial conditions. Watch energy and angular momentum stay constant.

two-body.title: Two-body problem
two-body.body: Two bodies orbiting a common centre of mass. The cleanest test of the integrator.

star-replacement.title: Replace the Sun
star-replacement.body: Swap the Sun for another star and see which planets keep their orbits and which fly away.

asteroid-impact.title: Asteroid on a collision course
asteroid-impact.body: Launch an asteroid at Earth and read impact speed, energy in TNT and airburst/crater outcome.

black-hole.title: Black-hole flyby
black-hole.body: A test particle near a Newtonian black hole (approximation, no relativity). Orbit, plunge or escape.

chelyabinsk-2013.body: 19 m airburst over Russia, about 500 kt. Compare the energy the simulator computes with the published figure.

tunguska-1908.body: Siberian airburst that flattened forest. Size and speed are highly uncertain, shown as such.

chicxulub.body: The end-Cretaceous impact. Energy is order-of-magnitude only; see how large that is next to the others.

apophis.body: Near-Earth asteroid with a safe 2029 flyby. Orbit from catalog values; no collision is predicted.

halley.body: Highly eccentric comet (eв‰€0.97). Speed changes enormously between perihelion and aphelion.

sirius-a.body: Put a 2-solar-mass A star at the centre. Which planets survive, and how do the periods change?

betelgeuse.body: Replace the Sun with a red supergiant. Its mass is uncertain; the sandbox warns about planets inside it.

proxima-centauri.body: A 0.12 solar-mass red dwarf has too little gravity to hold the Solar System planets.

cygnus-x-1.body: Stellar-mass black hole of about 21 solar masses. Test particle orbits, Newtonian approximation.

sagittarius-a-star.body: The Milky Way’s central black hole, about 4 million solar masses. Orbits are fast and tight.

m87-star.body: A 6.5-billion-solar-mass black hole. An extreme gravitational parameter for the engine.

proxima-b.body: Planet in an 11-day orbit. Minimum mass only; see how fast it moves around its small star.

51-pegasi-b.body: The first hot Jupiter: a giant planet orbiting in 4 days at 0.05 AU.

trappist-1e.body: Rocky planet around an ultracool dwarf. A 6-day year at a tiny orbital distance.

55-cancri-e.body: Lava world orbiting in under a day. A very fast, tight orbit.

sim.title: Mission simulation
sim.intro: Fly the mission you designed, stage by stage. Everything here is computed from your mission document: the rocket, orbit, power, battery, Δv, link and instruments you chose decide what happens.
sim.disclaimer: Educational approximation, not professional flight dynamics. The simplifications are listed at the bottom of this page.

controls.seedHint: The seed fixes every random event. The same design and seed always give the same result, at any speed.
